title: The Lone Ranger
paragraphs: A masked Western hero and his companion Tonto travel the American frontier fighting injustice, protecting the innocent, and bringing criminals to the law while guarding the Ranger's identity.

Detroit-originated masked-Western radio drama built around the Lone Ranger and Tonto. Creation is best treated as collaborative: George W. Trendle supplied the core concept/business direction, James Jewell shaped early dramatic production, and Fran Striker developed the scripts and much of the mythology. Sources differ on January 30 versus January 31, 1933 for the debut convention. New/live production ended September 3, 1954; transcribed repeats continued into 1956, with sources differing on the exact final May 1956 rerun date.

GRH documents the program through WXYZ / Michigan Radio Network launch (January 31, 1933 to October 1, 1934) on [[org|org.4873e07a843601f0|Michigan Radio Network]], Mutual / Earle Graser era (October 2, 1934 to April 7, 1941) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Graser-Beemer transition (April 9, 1941 to April 16, 1941) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Brace Beemer / Mutual era (April 18, 1941 to May 1, 1942) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are George W. Trendle (creator on 1868 recordings, producer on 1769 recordings, writer on 691 recordings, executive producer on 59 recordings, performer on 12 recordings, and director on 4 recordings), [[person|john-todd|John Todd]] (performer on 1979 recordings), [[person|brace-beemer|Brace Beemer]] (performer on 1580 recordings, announcer on 282 recordings, commercial spokesman on 5 recordings, and narrator on 3 recordings), Fran Striker (writer on 1251 recordings, editor on 353 recordings, story editor on 47 recordings, performer on 13 recordings, author on 1 recording, and director on 1 recording), Fred Foy (announcer on 529 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and editor on 1 recording), Charles D. Livingstone (director on 505 recordings, producer on 57 recordings, performer on 3 recordings, editor on 2 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), and [[person|earle-graser|Earle Graser]] (performer on 438 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]] (aircheck from station), and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).
Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Outlaws and outlaw gangs, Cattle and ranching, Murder, Rail transport, Horses, and Gold.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including The Lone Ranger and early cooperative radio-network expansion, Children’s radio, cereal sponsorship, and mail-order premiums, and The Lone Ranger across the radio-to-television transition.
